CSTEP Training · for Approvers

Approve or return a request

Every traveller is mapped to an Approver. When they submit a tour proposal, event request or claim it comes to you: read it through, then sanction it — which issues its reference number — or return it with a reason so they can fix it.

Part 1 of 5

Your queue

Where requests waiting for your decision show up.

  1. 1Your dashboard — Needs you now
  2. 2Travel Claims → Approvals
QueueStep 1 of 2 · Your dashboard

Needs you now

Your dashboard counts what is in your queues — flagged Action required — and Needs you now lists each request awaiting your sanction, with a Review button.

You see a request because the traveller is mapped to you as Approver. Nobody else's requests reach you.

Travel Claims → DashboardReview
QueueStep 2 of 2 · Approvals

Your Queues — everything awaiting your approval

Travel Claims → Approvals opens your queue: one card per request — the form type, its ID, Awaiting your sanction, the purpose and project, the dates, and who filed it.

Filter by purpose, traveller or ID; Export CSV downloads the list. Review opens the request.

Travel Claims → ApprovalsReview
Part 2 of 5

Sanction a tour

Read the proposal through, then sanction it.

  1. 1Open the request
  2. 2Read it through
  3. 3Sanction this tour — the TIN is issued
TourStep 1 of 3 · Open the request

Your sanction is the sanction

The request opens with your decision panel on top: Sanction this tour, Return for correction or Reject.

Opening it is recorded — the Audit trail on the right now shows START_REVIEW by you, under the traveller's SUBMIT.

TourStep 2 of 3 · Read it through

What the traveller asked for

Read it before you decide: stations and stays, travel modes, departure and return times, transport and accommodation, and under Other the project it is debited to.

Check the dates, the project and that the services asked for fit the purpose.

TourStep 3 of 3 · Sanction

Sanctioned — the Tour TIN is issued

Sanction this tour approves it at once: status APPROVED and TIN issued: 0001/1026 — the Tour TIN that identifies the trip from here on.

It moves on to the CSTEP Admin / Official to arrange, and the audit trail records your APPROVE.

Part 3 of 5

Approve a claim

Local travel and expense claims come to you the same way.

  1. 1Open the claim
  2. 2Check the lines and totals
  3. 3Approve this claim — the reference is issued
ClaimStep 1 of 3 · Open the claim

A claim in your queue

A claim opens with the same decision panel — the button reads Approve this claim.

Its lines show underneath: each trip with its fare, marked Bill or No bill.

ClaimStep 2 of 3 · Check the lines

Lines, food and totals

Check each trip and meal, and the Totals (as claimed): travel, food, other expenses, total claimed and any advance.

Trips with No bill are on the traveller's declaration; the CSTEP Admin checks every line against its bill at verification.

ClaimStep 3 of 3 · Approve

Approved — the claim reference is issued

Approve this claim: status APPROVED with its claim reference — here LTC0001/1026 (an Expense Claim gets EXP…, an Event Request EVR…).

The banner says where it goes next: now with the CSTEP Admin for verification, then Finance reimburses.

Part 4 of 5

Return or reject

Send it back to be fixed — or, rarely, close it for good.

  1. 1Return for correction — with your reason
  2. 2What the request shows afterwards
  3. 3Reject — and why to prefer Return
ReturnStep 1 of 3 · Return

Return for correction — say what to fix

Return for correction opens a box for your reason — it is required. Say exactly what needs changing.

Then Confirm return.

Return for correctionWrite the reasonConfirm return
ReturnStep 1 of 3 · Return

Returned — the reason goes with it

The request shows RETURNED and a Returned for correction notice with your name and reason. The audit trail records the RETURN with the same text.

It is back with the traveller to edit and resubmit — no reference number is issued until you sanction it.

ReturnStep 2 of 3 · Reject

Reject closes it for good

Reject asks for a reason too, and warns you: rejecting closes the request for good — the traveller cannot edit or resubmit it.

Use Return for correction whenever it only needs changes. (Here we stop before Confirm rejection.)

ReturnStep 3 of 3 · Your queue

What is left in your queue

Sanctioned, approved and returned requests leave your queue; only what still needs your decision stays.

Here one tour is still awaiting your sanction.

Part 5 of 5

Back from the requester

What the traveller sees after a return, and how it comes back to you.

  1. 1It waits on the requester
  2. 2They read your reason
  3. 3They fix it and resubmit
  4. 4It is back in your queue
ResubmitStep 1 of 4 · Waiting on them

The requester: waiting on you

On the traveller's dashboard the returned request counts as Waiting on you and sits at Draft / Returned in the pipeline.

Needs you now lists it as Needs correction — resubmit, with a Continue button.

ResubmitStep 2 of 4 · Your reason

They read your reason

The request shows the Returned for correction notice with your reason, and an Edit button.

The audit trail shows your RETURN, with the reason, under their original submission.

ResubmitStep 3 of 4 · Fix & resubmit

They fix what you asked for

Edit reopens the form with everything they filed. Here the traveller adds the venue and the lunch count you asked for.

Then Submit for approval again.

ResubmitStep 3 of 4 · Fix & resubmit

Resubmitted — every change recorded

The status is SUBMITTED again. The audit trail shows RESUBMIT, and each field they changed — here Changed eventVenue, from blank to the new venue — marked as a traveller edit.

You can see exactly what changed since you returned it.

ResubmitStep 4 of 4 · Back to you

Back in your queue

The request is back in your queue, Awaiting your sanction. Open it, check the changes, and sanction it — or return it again.

Reference

Your three decisions

What each button does, and when to use it.

DecisionUse whenWhat happensCan the traveller fix it?
Sanction / ApproveThe request is right as filedStatus APPROVED; reference issued (TIN, LTC, EXP or EVR); on to the CSTEP Admin / Official—
Return for correctionSomething needs changingStatus RETURNED with your reason; waits on the travellerYes — edit and resubmit; every change is recorded
RejectIt should not go ahead at allClosed for good, with your reasonNo — it cannot be edited or resubmitted
Recap

You can approve and return

Your queue
Dashboard → Needs you now, or Travel Claims → Approvals. Only travellers mapped to you reach you.
Read before you decide
Opening a request is recorded. Check dates, project, services or claim lines.
Sanction issues the reference
TIN for a tour, LTC / EXP for a claim, EVR for an event.
Return, don't reject
Return with a clear reason when it can be fixed; reject only to close it for good.
